previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 58-year-old woman was admitted due to confusion, tremor, double vision, and nausea following a recent hospital discharge, where her phenytoin dose had been increased. Her phenytoin level was found to be supratherapeutic at 22.2, consistent with toxicity, likely exacerbated by improved absorption from reduced bowel edema after diuresis and interactions with warfarin. She was evaluated by neurology, transitioned from phenytoin to levetiracetam (Keppra), and monitored with EEG, which showed no seizure activity. Symptoms gradually improved over the admission. Her INR was subtherapeutic at 1.9, prompting an increase in warfarin from 5 mg to 8 mg daily, with INR stabilizing at 2.1 by discharge. She received supportive care for chronic conditions including heart failure, fibromyalgia, and hypokalemia. Physical therapy confirmed safe ambulation. She was discharged home with home services, medication changes, and follow-up plans.

Patient presented with SCr of 1.0, her baseline level. After

Discharge Instructions:
Dear Ms. ___,

You were admitted to ___ 
with lower extremity swelling as well as redness of the left 
lower leg. Due to concern of cellulitis we treated you with an 
intravenous antibiotic called Vancomycin. You were treated with 
this medication for seven days with improvement of the redness 
in your left leg.

In order to treat your swelling, we attempted to diurese you. We 
stopped your home diuretics and gave you intravenous lasix as 
well as a lasix drip. We were able to drain fluid which was 
noted with decreased swelling and decreased weaping from the 
legs. We also encouraged the use of ACE wraps to improve the 
swelling in your legs. Unfortunately to prevent damage to your 
kidneys, we could not completely remove all of the fluid from 
your legs. We did obtain an ultrasound of your heart 
(echocardiogram) as well as a lab test to look for heart 
failure. These tests did not reveal heart failure.

We recommend you follow-up with your primary care physician to 
determine the appropriate diuresis to decrease swelling in your 
legs. We also recommend following up with the ___ clinic 
at ___ for further evaluation of your 
swelling. 

Also, please weigh yourself every morning and call your primary 
care physician if your weight goes up more than three pounds in 
a day for further evaluation and management.    

It was a pleasure taking care of you during your 
hospitalization.

Sincerely, 
Your ___ Care Team
